incident: check-claude-md-length.ps1, and by extension every other hook wired into school-admissions-assistant/.claude/settings.json (check-secrets, protect-rules, check-dangerous, check-code, from the earlier M06 build), never fired despite being correctly configured and syntactically valid.
root_cause: school-admissions-assistant/ has no .git of its own — C:\Users\Oggu\Documents\Tulip is the real repo root. Claude Code's hook discovery is scoped to that root, so the nested settings.json was silently never read. Confirmed by adding a debug hook that dumped the raw stdin payload to disk on both PreToolUse and PostToolUse, then triggering real Write/Edit calls — the debug file was never created either time.
fix: Moved all hooks into the repo-root .claude/settings.json. Each Admin-specific script now checks file_path for a school-admissions-assistant/ prefix before acting, so it doesn't misfire on Tulip's own files.
lesson: A hook or settings.json existing on disk with valid JSON is not evidence it's active. Always trigger a real bad action and confirm the block actually happens before trusting a sensor — config that's never exercised is indistinguishable from config that doesn't exist. Verify at the project's actual root boundary (git root), not wherever the file happens to sit.
